interpretation: Hips appears once in each of eight poems. Its contexts include city architecture, weather, music, childhood, remembered adulthood, burial work, and displacement. In “Buried,” the father moves his hips while digging a grave. In “Golden Rule Days,” hips describes Carla’s donated denims. The descriptions below are interpretations grounded in the poems.

occurrences.title: Prologue—And Then She Owns You
occurrences.subject: New Orleans, personified as a woman
occurrences.context: The city seduces the visiting you. Brick makes its erotic body architectural; rhumba and swerve make the attraction rhythmic.

occurrences.title: 5 P.M., Tuesday, August 23, 2005
occurrences.subject: Women, as described by the speaking storm
occurrences.context: The emerging storm connects female bodily self-knowledge with weather, appetite, and chaos. Katrina speaks; the phrase itself concerns every woman.

occurrences.title: Why New Orleans Is
occurrences.subject: Southern Illinois women performing karaoke in New Orleans
occurrences.context: Toned visiting bodies keep time to Black music. The poem sets their dancing and sexual release within a city they can consume and leave.

occurrences.title: Ms. Thang Sloshes in the Direction of Home
occurrences.subject: Ms. Thang
occurrences.context: Her shoes fail in flood mud, but she retains her sashay and treats movement as performance. Hips link bodily progress and feminine self-presentation under pressure.

occurrences.title: Thankful
occurrences.subject: The speaking we remembering childhood
occurrences.context: Children dance or play to rhymes while their mothers watch and warn them. Remembered bodily joy and care answer an official account of poverty that diminishes their former lives.

occurrences.title: 34, section 29
occurrences.subject: An older female nursing-home victim’s voice
occurrences.context: The speaker recalls sexual energy, style, motherhood, and belonging before accusing Louisiana of betrayal. Her remembered body supplies an individual life beyond a death count.

occurrences.title: Buried
occurrences.subject: The bereaved father digging a grave
occurrences.context: Jazz rhythm organizes strenuous digging. A body part previously associated with erotic dance now moves through exhausting burial work and grief.

occurrences.title: Golden Rule Days, section III
occurrences.subject: The hip area of Carla’s donated denims
occurrences.context: Ill-fitting donated clothing marks the displaced schoolchild for hostile recognition. The grammar attaches their to the denims; the image concerns clothing and social labeling.
